clue.text: Bandit ("The Knife") in one of 1 down in Spain

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside the sin named by the cross-reference

parts.note: sloth (laziness) is one of the seven deadly sins
Mack the Knife, of the song, gives his name Mac
taken as written
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A bandit nicknamed The Knife commits one of the deadly sins somewhere in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: Mack the Knife is the gangster of a famous song; 'one-armed bandit' is the nickname of a gambling machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambling machine with a lever is nicknamed a one-armed bandit because it takes your money.

clue.text: Fatal flaws — 2 minus 1?

parts.note: fatal flaws are the mortal failings of theology; 2 down is a group of eight, so taking one away leaves a count of seven

explanation.surface: Someone muses on deadly weaknesses and a puzzling sum.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is to OCTET at 2 down: eight minus one gives the number at the front, while 'Fatal flaws' covers the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional list of cardinal vices that lead to damnation numbers seven: pride, envy, wrath, sloth, greed, gluttony and lust.

clue.text: Musicians and the like upheld in scriptures

indicators.note: in places the turned piece inside the scriptures

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament

indicators.note: held up, in a down clue, means the piece is read from bottom to top

parts.note: etc, et cetera, means and the like

explanation.surface: Musicians and similar folk are honoured in holy writings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upheld' turns ETC, which then sits inside OT; in a down clue upheld means read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of eight musicians playing together is a classic chamber ensemble.

clue.text: Forced terrorists to drink

parts.note: made someone do something means forced them
the IRA, the Irish Republican Army

explanation.surface: Terrorists compelled someone to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortified wine from the Portuguese island of that name is a drink.

clue.text: Bunch featuring many a perpetrator of one of 1 down

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100, a crossword many

parts.words: a perpetrator of one of 1 down
parts.note: lust is a deadly sin, so one who commits it is a luster

explanation.surface: A gathering includes many people guilty of a deadly sin.
explanation.definitionFit: A cluster is a group of things together, a synonym of bunch.

clue.text: Rise lest soldiers invade

indicators.note: invading soldiers get inside, so they enter the other phrase

parts.note: lest means in case
RE, Royal Engineers, is the British army corps

explanation.surface: Someone warns that troops might invade.
explanation.definitionFit: A rise and an increase both mean a growth in amount.

clue.text: Greenly press hands with Lofty, consumed by one of 1 down

indicators.note: being eaten up by something puts the run of pieces inside the sin

parts.note: envy is one of the seven deadly sins
to iron clothes is to press them
workers, as in farm hands, are men
lofty means tall

explanation.surface: A man nicknamed Lofty is eaten up with envy while pressing clothes with his hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumed by' is the containment signal. Envy is the green-eyed monster, so a green surface hides the eco sense of Greenly.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenly in the ecological sense means in an eco-friendly way.

clue.text: Having mechanical sex with accountants, raised plant

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the whole run reads upwards

parts.note: AI, artificial insemination, is conception without intercourse
CA is a chartered accountant; two of them give CA twice

explanation.surface: A plant is lifted up while a racy scene with accountants unfolds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns AI plus CA and CA to give the plant. The racy picture is a joke: the sex is artificial insemination.
explanation.definitionFit: The wattle or thorn tree is a genus of flowering plant.

clue.text: Finally shed a tear about burning

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so a rent goes around the letter

parts.note: a rent is a tear in fabric

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word shed

explanation.surface: Someone finally sheds a tear over a fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' takes D from 'shed'; 'about' puts A RENT around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Burning passion and ardent passion are the same; both mean fervent.

clue.text: Teaching boys and girls to cover screen, 25-d in one of 1 down

indicators.note: covering something means going round it, so the teaching word wraps the screen word

parts.note: coed is coeducational, teaching both sexes together
to vet candidates is to screen them

explanation.surface: Mixed teaching is meant to screen what pupils do.
explanation.walkthrough: '25-d' means 25 across plus D: INDULGED. Indulged in covetousness (one of the deadly sins) is coveted.
explanation.definitionFit: To covet is to crave what another has, the sin of covetousness; something coveted is desired that way.

clue.text: Reveal Caledonian's very, very short

parts.note: unco is Scots for very

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written before cutting

explanation.surface: A Scot says something very, very briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts Y from VERY. Caledonian means Scottish.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncover something is to reveal it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Cheats cheated, by the sound of it, and put pressure on

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the words are heard, not spelt

parts.note: cons is a word for cheats, and tricked means cheated

explanation.surface: Swindlers were swindled and squeezed.
explanation.definitionFit: Constrict means squeeze or compress, putting pressure on something.

clue.text: Jane keeps one in the nest

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so the heroine contains the letter

parts.note: Jane Eyre, the Charlotte Brontë heroine
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Jane looks after one in the nest.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle's high nest has a special name; it stands for the nest.

clue.text: Elderly painter largely rejected

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word is read backwards
largely means most of it, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Edgar Degas, the French Impressionist

explanation.surface: An old painter is mostly turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' cuts DEGAS to DEGA; 'rejected' turns it back.
explanation.definitionFit: Elderly and aged both describe someone who is old.

clue.text: Untouchable Costa Ricans want one badly

indicators.note: badly signals the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Central Americans are desperate for something they cannot have.
explanation.walkthrough: 'want' means lack: rearrange COSTARICANS without I.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacrosanct means too sacred to be touched or criticised, so untouchable.

clue.text: Answer thus to one in town

parts.note: so means thus

indicators.note: in puts the numeral inside the town

parts.note: Luton, a town in Bedfordshire, England
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An answer is directed to someone in town.
explanation.walkthrough: Luton is an English town north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A solution is the answer to a problem or puzzle.

clue.text: Farewell note in cable — it reveals the inner man

indicators.note: in places the goodbye and note inside the cable

parts.note: a rope is a thick cable
adios is Spanish for goodbye
C is a musical note

explanation.surface: A goodbye message arrives in a telegram, about an instrument that sees inside people.
explanation.walkthrough: Cable sounds like a telegram; here it is a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: An X-ray viewing device shows the interior of the body, so it reveals what is inside a person.

clue.text: Officer showing resistance to one of 1 down

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance
anger, or wrath, is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: An officer shows resistance to a deadly sin.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranger is an officer who patrols a park or forest.

clue.text: Loose woman in bed, bedded with energy

indicators.note: in places one bed inside the other

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
bedded is read as a bed itself, a second cot laid inside the first
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A loose woman is in bed, bedded energetically.
explanation.walkthrough: One COT goes inside another, giving COCOTT, then E.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocotte is an old French-derived word for a promiscuous woman or prostitute.

clue.text: Supply nothing against getting into one of 1 down

indicators.note: getting into means entering, so the pieces go inside the sin

parts.note: pride is one of the seven deadly sins
O is zero, nothing
V for versus, against

explanation.surface: Someone supplies nothing in opposition to vanity.
explanation.definitionFit: Provide and supply both mean to give what is needed.

clue.text: Bird lover died in the field

indicators.note: in puts the letter inside the field

parts.note: a lea is a poetic word for a meadow

explanation.surface: A lover of birds died out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Zeus came to Leda as a swan, so she was a bird's lover, not a birdwatcher.
explanation.definitionFit: Leda was seduced by Zeus in the form of a swan, making her a bird's lover.

clue.text: Went along with article on one of 1 down

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
greed, or avarice, is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: Someone accepted an article about avarice.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so A comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To have agreed is to have gone along with a proposal.

clue.text: Buoyant heart befuddled by liqueur

indicators.note: befuddled means muddled up, so the letters are rearranged
heart means the word without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A cheerful spirit is muddled by a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' gives UOYAN from 'Buoyant'; 'befuddled' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Noyau is a French brandy liqueur flavoured with fruit kernels.

clue.text: Dull job involving first King's Singer

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the job contains the ordinal

parts.note: a chore is a tedious task
1st written out is IST
R is Rex, king

explanation.surface: A dull task was the first given to a royal singer.
explanation.walkthrough: King's College Cambridge has a famous choir, adding to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorister is a singer in a choir, especially a church choir.

clue.text: Waterway showing diligence without endeavour

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the effort word is removed

parts.note: industry means hard work, diligence
a try is an attempt, an endeavour

explanation.surface: A canal shows hard work but no effort.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indus is a great river of Pakistan, a waterway.

clue.text: Snobbish model is wearing hat backwards

indicators.note: backwards means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: tile is slang for a hat
is is taken as written; wearing says the hat sits on top, so it comes first
the Model T Ford gives T

explanation.surface: A snooty fashion model wears her hat back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' links: the hat sits on top, so its turned letters come first. Tile is old slang for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: An elitist favours a select few, so is snobbish.

clue.text: Eluding alternative humour

indicators.note: an alternative arrangement means the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Dodging the other kind of comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'humour' is the verb, to go along with someone's whims.
explanation.definitionFit: To humour someone is to indulge them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Understands about grinding lens with cunning, but without reason

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the seeing word goes round the ground lens

parts.note: sees means understands, as in I see

indicators.note: grinding a lens reshapes it, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: sly means cunning

explanation.surface: Someone grasps lens-grinding with cleverness, yet acts irrationally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grinding' scrambles LENS into NSEL; 'about' puts that inside SEES.
explanation.definitionFit: Senselessly means irrationally, without good sense or reason.
